_comments: #252: reviewers asked why Actual Close Date and Closed At both exist, and a rep looking for an
expected close date typed one into Actual Close Date on an open deal. The columns had no
description, so nothing on screen said which date is which or who writes it.
Closed At is the instant the close ran; Actual Close Date is the business day it closed on, in the
deal company's time zone. Sales.CloseDeal writes both, Sales.ReopenDeal clears both, and
AutoUpdateDescription goes to 0 because the columns carry no extended property: CodeGen's schema
sync rewrites Description from the column when the flag is on, and would put NULL back.

fields.Description: The moment the deal was closed. Set by closing the deal and cleared by reopening it; it cannot be edited. For when an open deal is expected to close, use Expected Close Date.

The business day the deal closed on, in its company's time zone. Set by closing the deal and cleared by reopening it; it cannot be edited. For when an open deal is expected to close, use Expected Close Date.
The user who closed the deal. Set by closing the deal and cleared by reopening it; it cannot be edited.
The day the deal is expected to close. Update it as the date moves; the actual close date is set when the deal is closed.
